note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count and address below comes from one City of Spokane page - its Recreational Fields and Sports page, whose "Tennis and Pickleball Courts" section holds three lists: tennis courts, tennis courts striped for pickleball, and dedicated pickleball courts. That page answers every scripted request with a redirect into a "Checking Your Browser" interstitial, so it was read in a browser on 7 September 2026 and saved as text with a header stating the method, as Cary's and Wichita's pages were. Where the City stays silent - on hours, lighting, surface, price, parking, and whether any court is indoors or out - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: The City of Spokane publishes nothing about parking at any of these six parks. The word does not appear anywhere in the City's section - no lot, no capacity, no fee, no permit - and this site does not fill that in from a map. What the City does give you is a house-number address for every park, and every one of the six resolves as written. A.M. Cannon Park at 1511 N Elm St and Peaceful Valley Park at 1602 W Water Ave are both in 99201; Mission Park at 1208 E Mission Ave and Underhill Park at 2910 E Hartson Ave are both in 99202; Comstock Park at 601 W 29th Ave is in 99203 on the South Hill, and Corbin Park at 2914 N West Oval St is in 99205. Three of those addresses are worth a note, because the imported dataset this site was built from held them differently: Comstock at "3012 S Howard St", Peaceful Valley at a street range, "100-198 N Maple St", and Corbin at "501 West Park Place". The City's addresses replace all three. For Comstock and Corbin the old address is another side of the same park, so an old map search still gets you there; where to leave the car, nobody has published.
slots.peak_hours: The City states no hours for any of these courts and no lighting at any of them, so this page cannot say when a Spokane court opens, closes or goes dark. What the City does state is how you get on one, in one sentence for every court in the section: "Tennis & Pickleball courts are first-come-first-served, however if you would like to officially reserve a court and receive a reservation permit please fill out the online form." Turning up is the normal way in at all six parks, with no sign-up sheet and no booking system published. And a court you arrive at may be under a permit, because someone else has filled in the form; the City publishes no calendar of permits, no lead time and no price. Then there is who else uses the ground. At four of the six parks the pickleball courts are lines on tennis courts, and the City opens the section with what those tennis courts are for: they "host neighborhood pick-up games, parks and recreation classes and many tennis events". Thirty-two of Spokane's thirty-six pickleball courts sit on that shared ground, so a tennis class or event at Mission or Comstock is a class or event on the pickleball courts too. Only Corbin Park's two courts and Underhill Park's two are on the City's "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" list, pickleball whenever you arrive. When any of this is busy, the City does not say, and that silence is left as it is.
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface for any court in Spokane, and says nothing about condition, resurfacing, cracks or the state of the lines. What it does distinguish, precisely, is the kind of court you are walking onto. The heading "Tennis Courts Striped for Pickleball" covers four of the six parks and thirty-two of the thirty-six courts: A.M. Cannon with two, Comstock with twelve, Mission with sixteen and Peaceful Valley with two. Set beside the City's "Tennis Courts" list, the layouts show through. Comstock has six tennis courts and twelve pickleball courts, Mission eight and sixteen, Peaceful Valley one and two - two pickleball courts to a tennis court at all three. A.M. Cannon has two tennis courts and two pickleball courts, one to one. The tennis number is the number of slabs you are sharing. The heading "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" covers Corbin Park and Underhill Park, two courts each, built for the game rather than lined onto it; Corbin also keeps one tennis court on the tennis list, and Underhill appears on no list but the pickleball one. Nets are not mentioned anywhere in the section, so whether a striped court has a net at pickleball height is a question the City has not answered.
slots.local_scene: Thirty-six verified courts across six City parks: thirty-two striped on tennis courts and four dedicated. Mission Park's sixteen, on the eight tennis courts in the Logan neighbourhood, is the largest set in the city, and Comstock Park's twelve on six on the South Hill is the second; the other four parks hold two courts each. Spokane is the fifth Washington city published here, the first east of the Cascades and the first in Spokane County. Its page could not be read by machine: my.spokanecity.org answers every scripted fetch with a redirect into a "Checking Your Browser" interstitial, so the section was read in a browser and saved as text, and every line of it is asserted on every build. The City names no club, no league and no open-play group; its one sentence about who plays is about tennis courts that "host neighborhood pick-up games, parks and recreation classes and many tennis events". Nothing on the page says any court is free. The imported dataset this site was built from carried "Free public play" against Comstock, Mission and Peaceful Valley; the City writes no price and no "free", so those notes are gone and every venue here reads as unstated on cost. The same dataset held Comstock at four courts; the City says twelve. One park the City lists is not published, and it is named here rather than dropped. Sky Prairie Park appears on the striped list as "Sky Prairie Park, 8501 N. Nettleton Ct., 2 Courts", and that address resolves at no house number in either resolver this site uses, the Census geocoder or OpenStreetMap. The refusal is on the address alone, and the build is written to fail the day the address resolves. Grant Park, which the imported dataset carried as a pickleball venue, is on the City's tennis list only, so it is not here either.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts in one place
best_for.text: Mission Park holds sixteen pickleball courts, striped on the eight tennis courts in the Logan neighbourhood - the largest set in Spokane, two pickleball courts to a tennis court. First-come-first-served, with a reservation permit by online form. The City states no hours, lighting, surface or price, and tennis decides how many of the sixteen are yours.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a court that is pickleball whenever you arrive
best_for.text: Underhill Park has two courts on the City's "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" list and none on its tennis list, so it is the one park in Spokane where the pickleball courts share their ground with nothing. First-come-first-served, with a reservation permit by online form; nothing stated on hours, lights, surface or price.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a large set on the South Hill
best_for.text: Comstock Park holds twelve pickleball courts on six tennis courts, the second-largest set in the city. The imported dataset had it at four courts on another street; the City's list says twelve at 601 W 29th Ave. Shared with tennis, first-come-first-served, nothing stated on hours, lighting or price.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Spokane have?
faqs.a: We have verified 36 across six City parks: sixteen at Mission Park, twelve at Comstock Park, and two each at A.M. Cannon, Peaceful Valley, Corbin and Underhill. Thirty-two are stripes on tennis courts and four are dedicated. The City lists a seventh park, Sky Prairie, at an address that does not resolve.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Spokane?
faqs.a: Not stated. The City says the courts are first-come-first-served and that a court can be officially reserved with a reservation permit by online form; it names no price for the permit and never says the courts are free, so cost reads as unstated at every venue.

faqs.q: Which Spokane courts have lights, and what are the hours?
faqs.a: The City states neither. No hours appear in the section and no lighting does either, so every venue here reads as not verified on lighting - a gap in what the City writes down, not a claim that the courts are dark.

faqs.q: What does "Tennis Courts Striped for Pickleball" mean?
faqs.a: That the pickleball courts are lines painted on tennis courts and shared with tennis. The City's tennis list gives the slab count and its striped list the pickleball count: Comstock six and twelve, Mission eight and sixteen, Peaceful Valley one and two, A.M. Cannon two and two.

faqs.q: Why is Sky Prairie Park not listed?
faqs.a: The City lists it with two pickleball courts at "8501 N. Nettleton Ct.", and that address resolves at no house number in the Census geocoder or OpenStreetMap. A venue publishes here with an address that resolves as written, and none is taken from outside the operator. The build fails the day the address resolves.
